stdio_review.algorithm_assessment: Extract the cactus cycles with iterative DFS; each tree edge belongs to at most one extracted cycle. Process the resulting blocks bottom-up. A bridge combines two branch heights normally. In a cycle, two attached branches have shortest-path distance equal to their heights plus the smaller circular separation; a doubled-array monotone deque tests every pair with separation at most half the cycle in linear time. Update the attachment-root height using shortest circular distances, preserving previously combined branches at shared articulation vertices.
stdio_review.limitations: One source reviewer plus actual isolated tests, not independent dual semantic review.

stdio_review.algorithm_assessment: The maximum distinct membership patterns equals the number of cells formed by m generic central hyperplanes on an n-dimensional sphere:2*sum_{i=0..n}C(m-1,i). The central-arrangement recurrence follows by adding one great sphere and counting the cells cut on it. Stereographic projection maps these great spheres to ordinary sphere boundaries in R^n; flipping an individual inside/outside bit if needed preserves the number of patterns. For n=1 the two unbounded interval components share one pattern, correctly giving2m rather than2m+1. Use exact integers and cap the binomial index when n>=m-1.
